value.rationale: Bilateral sketch singular-value gaps are used for numerical-rank detection (Meier–Nakatsukasa). A rank-two matrix with one vanishing singular value is the natural smallest benchmark. The exact equal-dimension logarithmic tail, asymmetric no-log tail, and if-and-only-if two-sided oversampling requirement for finite normalized second moment separate measurable reliability regimes missed by generic embedding bounds. This is a structural quantitative law rather than an arbitrary entrywise special case; finite-gap and other-distribution limitations are explicitly stated.
